第 74 章 “Remote”「远程」

Silvia Botros / 西尔维娅·博特罗斯

— 第 205 页 —

I never liked that term "remote." It is exclusionary. And betrays a sense of "otherness" that I feel is unhealthy for team cohesion. I understand that not everyone finds it easy or productive to work mostly apart from daily, in-person, social interaction. But success is an arm-in-arm effort, and the strategies to build successful teams work regardless of geography if we reward the appropriate behaviors.

我从不喜欢「远程」这个词。它是排他的。它背叛了一种「他者」感，我觉得那对团队凝聚力不健康。我理解不是每个人都觉得在很大程度上脱离日常面对面社交互动工作容易或高效。但成功是一个挽臂并肩的努力，建立成功团队的策略不管地理位置都有效，如果我们奖励合适的行为。

I work remotely and have been for a few years since a couple of family moves. It has been a mostly successful experience this time around. What I do not talk about often is the story of when I didn't succeed as a remote employee, resulting in being laid off years ago. And I think it's important to talk about that, as well. Because as gratifying as it might be to claim full credit at my current success, I'd be dishonest to pretend that success was all me. So, what is it that makes the same person excel or fail miserably at the same thing? Let me share some of my experience around this and how I think it might matter to your organization.

我远程工作，因为几次家庭搬家已经几年了。这次是大体成功的体验。我不常谈的是我作为远程员工不成功、几年前被裁员的故事。我觉得谈那个也很重要。因为虽然把现在的成功全归功于自己可能令人满足，但假装成功全是我一个人是不诚实的。那是什么让同一个人在同一件事上要么出色要么惨败？让我分享一些这方面的经验，以及我觉得它可能和你的组织有什么关系。

The Team团队

There is never a "successful remote employee." There is always a "team that communicates well" and this goes beyond locality and who's physically where. I've seen engineering teams in the same office fail spectacularly at basic communication around work in progress or around setting expectations for delivering feature work, whereas other teams spanning three different time zones efficiently produce results. This is all a roundabout way for me to say that my success is really my team's success. There are a number of habits that make my team so good at this and they are worth calling out:

从来没有「成功的远程员工」。总是有「沟通良好的团队」，这超越了地理位置和谁物理上在哪里。我见过同一办公室的工程团队在关于在途工作或设定交付功能工作期望的基本沟通上惨败，而跨三个不同时区的其他团队高效产出结果。这一切都是我绕着弯说我的成功其实是我团队的成功。有一些习惯让我的团队在这方面这么好，值得指出：

  • Most conversations happen in chat, keeping everyone in the loop.大多数对话在聊天中发生，让每个人都在圈子里。
  • Joining standups from laptops, even for those in the office. Everyone is on the same communication channels.用笔记本电脑参加站会，即使在办公室的人也是。每个人都在同样的沟通渠道上。
— 第 206 页 —
  • In meetings where a large portion of the group is in a big room, someone is designated as representative of those calling in. That way we can still get the group's attention and ask questions if we want to.在大部分人在大房间开会时，指定一个人作为电话接入者的代表。这样我们如果想仍然能引起群体注意和提问。

These are not just behaviors that are useful when the entire team isn't local. Life happens, coworkers have to work from home sometimes, errands, all sorts of things. Allowing for your people to still be part of important discussions while living life is a real sign of wanting life balance for your people and not just talking about it.

这些不只是整个团队不在本地时有用的行为。生活在发生，同事有时候得在家工作、跑腿、各种事情。让你的人在过生活时仍然能参与重要讨论，是真正想让你的人有工作生活平衡的标志，而不只是嘴上说说。

The Effects of Human Laziness人类懒惰的影响

Humans are by nature lazy: we do not seek what we do not see. And we make presumptions about things we do not know for a fact. These natural shortcuts our brains take will always show themselves in the systems we design. I have seen it multiple times where teams have developed and deployed software that did not actually meet all the needs of the business only for retrospectives later to declare the "root cause" a failure in communication.

人类天生懒惰：我们不寻找我们看不到的东西。我们对不确定的事情做假设。我们大脑走的这些自然捷径总会在我们设计的系统中表现出来。我多次见过团队开发和部署的软件其实没有满足业务的所有需求，只是后来在回顾会上宣布「根本原因」是沟通失败。

It amazes me how often organizations will over and over again prove Conway's law in this specific dynamic. Teams that communicate only to humans in front of them will also fail to involve all stakeholders in decisions in design, will fail to notify other teams when they are about to ratchet up customer involvement in their new beta, and will create products that ultimately are a reflection of how the team itself handles its communication. It has been my experience that teams that put the effort into being good at communication, at writing things down, and at making everything explicit, also find the most alignment and find all their members rowing in the same direction. Having people work from wherever they live at this point becomes the cherry on top.

让我惊讶的是组织多频繁地在这个特定动态中反复证明 Conway 定律。只和面前的人沟通的团队也会在设计决策中不涉及所有利益相关者，在他们即将提高新 beta 的客户参与度时不通知其他团队，并创造最终反映团队本身如何处理沟通的产品。根据我的经验，那些努力擅长沟通、写下来、让一切明确的团队，也找到最多对齐、发现所有成员朝同一方向划桨。让人在他们住的任何地方工作在这一点上就成了锦上添花。

Hiring, Diversity, and Inclusion招聘、多元化和包容

Here's a harsh truth: if you require hiring in a specific geographic location but pinky swear that you value diversity and inclusion, you are at best misguided as to how to create diverse teams and how to keep underrepresented groups included. Intent doesn't matter when hiring practices have the opposite impact.

这是一个残酷真相：如果你要求在特定地理位置招聘但小拇指发誓你重视多元化和包容，你在怎么创造多元化团队、怎么让代表性不足群体被包容方面最多是被误导。当招聘实践有相反影响时，意图不重要。

— 第 207 页 —

If you decide to open the experienced roles to "anywhere US" but none of your engineering managers have previously managed people not local to them or, worse, are not interested in that, you are hiring experienced engineers to see them fail. We are in an industry that has far more demand for talent than is available to hire. And that's an advantage for us as workers. I see companies clearly state hiring as a challenge and something that's a competitive edge, yet they hamstring those same efforts by requiring that people relocate. Not only does this make hiring more difficult, but it is also not inclusive.

如果你决定把有经验的岗位开放给「美国任何地方」但你的工程经理以前都没管理过不在本地的人，或者更糟，对此不感兴趣，你就是在招有经验的工程师来看他们失败。我们在一个人才需求远大于可招人才的行业。这对我们作为工作者是优势。我看到公司明确说招聘是挑战和竞争优势，但他们通过要求人搬家来束缚同样的努力。这不仅让招聘更难，也不包容。
